author: Animalogic
description:
Canids are some of the greatest predators on Earth. They have spread to almost every nook and cranny of the globe, with the exception of Antarctica and some islands. But their story is a long and complicated one. The entire lineage was close to extinction multiple times. So how did they make it? What adaptations helped them thrive across the world? And why are they quite simply the best? This is the 40 million-year story of the dog.

00:00 The 40 Million Year History of Dogs
01:01 Prohesperocyon: The First True Canid
03:10 Hesperocyon & The Hesperocyoninae Lineage
04:25 Tiny Foxes, Hypercarnivores, & Osbornodon
06:05 The Hypercarnivory Trap & The Rise of Cats
06:51 Borophaginae: The Bone-Crushers & Bear-Dogs
09:48 Leptocyon: The Survivor & Origin of All Modern Dogs
10:44 Eucyon & The First Dogs to Leave North America
11:39 Vulpes & The Foxy Canids Around the World
14:16 Canis & The Wolf-Like Canids
16:28 Extinct Wolves: The Sardinian Dhole & The Dire Wolf
17:36 South American Weirdos:
title: Why Did Dogs Go From That To This?
